evidence: src/business/services/ReceivingService.ts: constructor injects `ItemTable` and `BinTable`, then turns rows into domain objects with `new Item(...)` / `new Bin(...)` and uses `bin.put`, `bin.take`, `item.needsReorder`, `StockError`

src/business/services/CycleCountService.ts: constructor injects the raw `PrismaService` and calls `this.prisma.stockCount.create(...)` and `this.prisma.stockCount.findMany()` directly, without using any table gateway or the Bin domain object
src/business/services/CycleCountService.ts count(): `counted === expected ? null : { binCode, delta: counted - expected }`

src/business/services/CycleCountService.ts openDiscrepancies(): `rows.filter((r) => r.counted !== r.expected).map((r) => ({ binCode: r.binCode, delta: r.counted - r.expected }))`, which repeats the discrepancy rule from count()
src/business/services/ReceivingService.ts receive(): throws `StockError` when quantity is not a positive whole number; CycleCountService.count() does no matching check on `counted`
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Both services deal with warehouse stock, but they use different abstractions to do it. ReceivingService goes through the table gateways (ItemTable, BinTable) and turns rows into domain objects (Item, Bin), so domain logic sits in those objects: bin.put, bin.take, item.needsReorder, and StockError for failures. CycleCountService skips all of that. It takes the raw PrismaService client, calls prisma.stockCount.create and findMany directly, and works on plain rows. It never uses Bin or a table gateway, and it builds its own ID string. So the module mixes two styles: one goes through gateways and domain objects, the other writes straight to the ORM.

CycleCountService also writes the discrepancy rule twice. The test for a mismatch (counted vs expected) and the delta calculation (counted - expected) appear in both count() and openDiscrepancies(), when they should live in one place.

It also never validates its counted value. ReceivingService checks that quantities are valid and throws StockError when they are not, so the two services apply input checks unevenly.

violations.message: Skips the module's persistence and domain abstractions: it injects the raw PrismaService and calls prisma.stockCount.create/findMany on plain rows. ReceivingService instead uses the ItemTable/BinTable gateways and the Bin/Item domain objects, so the two services in this module are inconsistent.
The discrepancy rule (the counted vs expected mismatch test and delta = counted - expected) is written twice, in count() and openDiscrepancies(), instead of in one place.
